instructions: Set the 12 eggs on the counter about 20 minutes before you start. Fridge-cold eggs brown underneath before the top sets.
Heat the oven to 200°F and put 4 plates in to warm.
Finely chop 3 tbsp of the chives.

Crack the eggs into a large bowl and beat them with a fork until they're completely smooth, with no stringy bits of white left. Beat in the 3/4 tsp salt, the 1/4 tsp white pepper and 2 tbsp of the chopped chives.
Set an 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium low. Add 1 tsp of the butter and let it melt. It should foam gently without turning brown.

Pour in a quarter of the eggs, about 2/3 cup. Leave them for 30 seconds, then stir quickly with a silicone spatula or chopsticks while you shake the pan, until small soft curds form and the bottom starts to set, about 30 seconds more.
Stop stirring and smooth the top into an even layer. Put a lid on the pan for 45 seconds to 1 minute, until the top is just set but still glossy. The shorter time keeps the middle soft.
Tilt the pan away from you and roll the omelette from the handle side toward the far edge with the spatula, so you end up with a neat log. Tip it seam side down onto a warm plate.
Rub 1 tsp of the butter over the top and sprinkle on a little of the remaining chopped chives. Keep it in the oven while you make the rest.
Make the other 3 omelettes the same way, with 1 tsp of butter in the pan and 1 tsp rubbed on top each time. If the first one browned, turn the heat down a touch for the next.
Serve them hot, as soon as the last one is rolled.
method_notes: Both French versions keep it to eggs, butter and salt in a small nonstick pan over gentle heat, stirring to soft curds before the omelette is rolled and turned out seam side down with a little butter on top, pale with no browning. Not Quite Nigella sieves the eggs, adds chives and white pepper, and covers the pan for under a minute to set the top; Le Cordon Bleu uses clarified butter, folds it with a fork and shapes it into a torpedo under a towel. RecipeTin Eats' omelette is a softer folded, cheese-filled style with cream in the eggs, so this follows the lead's rolled method. Written as four 3-egg omelettes made one after another.
